The result is a transient eval infrastructure failure caused by provider capacity, not a confirmed defect in the session-share product surface. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-21T23:40–23:47Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable": the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never reached a running state, so the expected-output contract was entirely unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api) has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended-resource capacity on the 2 eligible nodes. The scheduler message "2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" and "2 No preemption victims found" confirms that no schedulable capacity remains and preemption cannot free any. The 4 remaining nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector, so they cannot serve as fallback. Because the pod never schedules, the agent VM is never provisioned, and all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) remain absent. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm in the production-api environment has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that match the required node affinity/selector. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. As a result, every attempt to schedule a remote-agent pod during this eval window was rejected as Unschedulable, preemption found no victims, and no agent VM was ever provisioned. This is a cluster-level infrastructure capacity constraint, not an eval runner or contract configuration defect. The failure is localized to the remote-agents feature in production-api and is confirmed as an eval-observed infrastructure failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: model-matrix eval failure: aura-gpt-5-5 returned HTTP 502 due to upstream Anthropic 429 rate-limit error
investigations.summary: The model-matrix observability eval failed because the runtime test call for model aura-gpt-5-5 received a 502 Bad Gateway response wrapping an Anthropic API 429 Too Many Requests (rate_limit_error). One of two configured models passed (aura-claude-sonnet-4-6), causing the allPassed and failedModelCount assertions in the expected-output contract to fail. This is an eval-layer signal of a transient upstream rate-limit condition; no user-traffic or incident evidence is present in the packet.
investigations.rootCause: The AURA runtime harness issued a POST to /api/agents/[REDACTED]/runtime/test for model aura-gpt-5-5 and received a 502 whose body contains a rate_limit_error from the Anthropic API (HTTP 429). The harness surfaced this as a bad_gateway error, the probe recorded ok: false for that model, and the model-matrix check consequently violated the allPassed === true and failedModelCount === 0 assertions defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json (line 333–334). The failure is localized to the aura-gpt-5-5 model slot in the desktop-release runtime path at the time of the eval run (2026-07-21T23:38:50Z–23:40:11Z). Whether this reflects a sustained provider-side rate limit, a misconfigured model routing that sends aura-gpt-5-5 traffic through the Anthropic provider unexpectedly, or a momentary spike is uncertain without additional run history or provider status data.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors reporting that 0 of 6 nodes could accept a new pod: 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never scheduled, no agent was created, and the runtime eval produced zero evidence — all 5 required fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are missing.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm in the production-api environment has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that match the required node affinity/selector. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. As a result, every attempt to schedule a remote-agent pod during this eval window was rejected as Unschedulable, preemption found no victims, and no agent VM was ever provisioned. This is a cluster-level infrastructure capacity constraint, not an eval runner or contract configuration defect. The failure is localized to the remote-agents feature in production-api and is confirmed as an eval-observed infrastructure failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary: The kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on the 2 affinity-matching nodes in the production-api cluster, leaving no schedulable capacity for new remote-agent pods. All three sibling checks hit this same wall independently (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

Secondary: The node affinity or selector on the remote-agent pod spec is too restrictive, limiting eligible nodes to only 2 out of 6, and those 2 are already saturated. If the affinity were broadened or additional matching nodes were added, capacity would increase.

Tertiary: A prior eval run or external workload may have left orphaned remote-agent pods running on the 2 eligible nodes, consuming all available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and preventing new scheduling. The withCleanup wrapper in the runner (run-status-probes.mjs line 1916) is intended to release resources, but a failed or interrupted prior run could have left pods unreclaimed.

Lower confidence: The node affinity/selector configuration on the pod template may have drifted from the actual node labels in the cluster, effectively reducing the eligible node pool from a larger set to only 2 nodes.
